scopeName: Integrate the hero-plus-merchant large-idle-game proposal into the Cat's Tower canonical product without breaking the cat-led identity, nine-screen contract, deterministic economy, or six-step evidence order.

governance.previousCanonicalSealRole: historical baseline for comparison; it does not authorize Step 2 while this change control is open

authoritativeInputs: the twenty user-provided images supplied to the 00_統括・工程管理 chat on 2026-08-26

acceptanceMatrix.condition: The revised one-line product identity makes the hero and merchant fantasies simultaneously legible while preserving cats as the visible protagonists and the player as the leader of a cat adventuring merchant company.
No generic human hero, external kingdom, or parallel adventure lobby displaces the one-tower cat-led product identity.
Combat, reinforcement, commerce, delivery, offline progress, and Dawn form one closed progression economy; no proposed subsystem becomes an isolated second game.
Spendable currencies remain current-run coin and permanent Dawn shard only. Reputation, blueprints, district badges, achievements, and restoration progress remain non-spendable state or unlock flags.

Gacha, pity, duplicate shards, premium gems, paid timer acceleration, random-stat equipment, inventory dismantling loops, forced advertisements, energy gates, and mandatory daily retention chores remain excluded from the core product.
evidenceRequired: explicit exclusion list in canonical spec

acceptanceMatrix.condition: The ten supplied concept families are mapped into the existing S01-S09 responsibilities without creating an undisclosed tenth canonical screen or five permanently competing navigation roots.

The battle screen keeps one dominant action and a readable frontline. Commerce support is visible through compact status and deliveries rather than a permanently expanded management dashboard covering the battle.
Auto battle begins early, active input is optional optimization, and no collect-all, restock, repeated level-one purchase, long hold, or high-frequency tap routine is required for baseline progress.

The 100-floor macro presentation remains a continuous living tower with district landmarks. A discrete node-map topology may be used only as a visual summary if it does not replace floor browsing or alter progression semantics.

Merchant management is converted into deterministic, auto-running shop placement, leveling, adjacency, and visible delivery effects. Manual collection, stock refill, restart timers, and opaque chain multipliers are prohibited.
Formation depth uses the existing named-cat and temporary-helper model. The first production district does not become a forty-character rarity collector or a five-slot generic hero party.
Forge depth is expressed through the existing one-at-a-time tower-wide armament families, deterministic tiers, and disclosed matchup forecasts; there is no random-stat item inventory.

Kingdom restoration is either rejected or translated into visual restoration of conquered tower districts. It must not add a separate town-building economy or timer layer to the current six-step scope.
Every changed executable semantic is propagated to candidate-v1.json, its schema, validators, input contract, deterministic simulator requirements, and a new Step 1 seal before Step 2 starts.
The active workflow status clearly blocks Steps 2-6 until this integration is resealed, while preserving Round 5 as immutable historical evidence rather than rewriting it.
At least three independent critics separately attack product identity, economy/simulation closure, and mobile UI density; all unresolved P0 and P1 findings are zero before PASS.

fixedDecisionsForThisRound: The current Round 5 canonical specification is the comparison baseline, not disposable legacy.
The integration is a Step 1 semantic change and therefore blocks Step 2.
The supplied screens are design proposals and audit inputs, not approved final mockups or production assets.
No runtime, asset, Vercel, branch, or production change is part of Round 1.

questionsToResolveBeforeCanonicalRedline.question: How is the hero fantasy named and shown without introducing a generic protagonist who displaces the cats?
questionsToResolveBeforeCanonicalRedline.proposedResolution: The player is the cat adventuring merchant company leader; the named cats are the visible adventurers and battle heroes.

questionsToResolveBeforeCanonicalRedline.question: How much merchant information remains visible during battle?
questionsToResolveBeforeCanonicalRedline.proposedResolution: Compact delivery/support status stays on S02; detailed production, placement, and comparison remains in S05/S07.

questionsToResolveBeforeCanonicalRedline.question: Does the 100F strategy-map proposal change topology?
questionsToResolveBeforeCanonicalRedline.proposedResolution: No. Preserve the continuous tower; use district landmarks and a compressed overview only as an S03 state.

questionsToResolveBeforeCanonicalRedline.question: Which proposed long-tail systems enter the current product?
questionsToResolveBeforeCanonicalRedline.proposedResolution: None of gacha, random equipment, town timers, dailies, seasons, ranking, premium acceleration, or social live operations enter the current six-step scope.

failureConditions: Step 2 begins before the integration has a new Step 1 PASS seal.
A tenth canonical screen is introduced without explicit scope revision.
Cats cease to be the visible protagonists.
A third spendable currency or premium acceleration is introduced.
The battle screen permanently exposes the full merchant dashboard.
A proposed feature is accepted solely because it appeared in a polished concept image.
Runtime, asset, or Vercel work begins during this documentation-only round.
Any write targets a branch other than kimi.
verificationEnvironment: live GitHub kimi branch at the exact recorded base commit
repository source-of-truth and Step 1 evidence review
manual inspection of all twenty supplied images
JSON parse validation for new machine-readable artifacts
